newsitem.title: USA: IMF to continue talks on Sudan next week.
newsitem.headline: IMF to continue talks on Sudan next week.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund on Tuesday delayed a decision on whether to take the first steps to expel Sudan until next week.
"The IMF executive board has extended its consideration of these issues until next week," an IMF spokesman said.
Sudan is $1.7 billion in arrears on its loan repayments to the IMF and has shown little interest in rescheduling or other measures to solve the problem, monetary sources said.

The IMF board has already held three days of discussions on the possible expulsion of Sudan. But it has been unable to reach a consensus on what to do, with industrial countries and developing nations lining up on opposite sides of the issue.

The IMF board, which is expected to take up the issue again on Feb. 12, could decide by a simple majority vote of 51 percent to recommend that the Fund's member countries expel Sudan from the lending agency.
But it would take an 85 percent vote of the IMF's 181 member nations to actually kick the African nation out.

While some countries have chosen to leave the lending institution voluntarily, IMF records show only one country -- Czechoslovakia -- was compelled to withdraw because it refused to provide required economic data in the early 1950s.
